Consequently, effective land use planning and control is required immediately if a proliferation of trailer parks and other ill-planned temporary facilities is to be avoided. If such developments spring up in the flood plain, or in areas where inadequate water supplies exist, or where adequate sewage treatment cannot be provided, they could present serious environmental hazards in addition to being an aesthetic blight.
The town of Lodge Grass is presently included in the area served by the Big Horn County Planning Board and is considering the adoption of a sub-division ordinance. Also, as discussed in Chapter II, the Crow Tribe has adopted a Environmental Health and Sanitation Ordinance, a Land Use Zoning Ordinance, a Law and Order Code and a Tribal Coal Taxation Code. Should these codes and ordinances be approved and implemented, undesirable forms of residential and commercial development may be controlled along the Little Bighorn valley within the Reservation.
Even with the implementation of Tribal controls there exists an urgent need for cooperation between Tribal, state, and county authorities aimed at joint, coordinated, comprehensive planning and land use controls. Delays caused by jurisdictional disputes or uncertainties could jeopardize the timely undertaking of planning and the imposition of effective controls on land use, to the detriment of all concerned.
